utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At the very outset, I'd like to apologise for the very late start. I had originally scheduled a start at 2.45, and now it is ten past 3.00. I do apologise. It is entirely due to the fact that I had duties to perform in my other role for the Tribunal. Now, Mr. Alarid, I understand you have a matter to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The only matter that -- for the session is just a notice that the Milutinovic Judgement is coming down tomorrow contemporaneous with our case as well; and, of course, both counsel in the room are participants in that and would like to be there. But the quandary is, of course, one of our witnesses is not here yet for tomorrow yet any way because of the plane crash at Schipol or whatever happened there and so that witness has been re-routed to Brussels and we're anticipating -- but it would be also be Mr. Ivetic' role to proof that witness as well two others. We had the three proofed for today so that wasn't a problem. We had anticipated actually all six being done in only two court sessions considering the brief nature of their testimony. So I was hoping on behalf of the other counsel in the room to request tomorrow afternoon off and/or rescheduled to the morning although that still provides some problems possibly with the proofing of witnesses. So I didn't know if the Court was going to be amenable to some sort of consideration of the Judgement coming down tomorrow afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Milutinovic starts when, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: 2.15, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You say Mr. Ivetic is involved in -- in relation to one of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. He has -- his role has been to proof the Serbian speaking witnesses and what-not, so you know because of course when I treat him solely as a translator, it slows things down. It is difficult to get through proofing sessions when he is created an intermediary. That is one of the primary roles as his duties here, as co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I am very reluctant to -- to be breaking again after a two-week break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And understood, Your Honour, I mean, on a push-comes-to-shove scenario, I could do the direct examination with my new legal assistant in the courtroom who speaks the language to assist me but I mean that would, you know, be a fallback position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I believe we would have to do with that position. I'm grateful to you, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I will accommodate the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have lost a tremendous amount of time in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and, you know, in the nature of trying to pair down the witness list other than outstanding matters with the experts and what-not, we are getting close to a point, I think, where we can focus the Defence case to a point where I think it needs to be so we have been trying to whittle down the witnesses as we speak. We are still going to finish in the time-frame allotted by the Court, if all goes well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a session tomorrow afternoon at 2.15. Let the witness be called.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is MLD21, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, number what, 11 or ... no, no, the number of the witnesses for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I will check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. You may sit, and you may begin, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir, as you know, my name is Mr. Ivetic and I am one of the attorneys for Milan Lukic in these proceedings. I'm going to have to refer to you today by your pseudonym of MLD21 in line with the protective measures that have been granted for you. With that in mind, and with the usher's assistance, I would like to show you a pseudonym sheet, and when that -- when you get a chance to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: There are some minor technical issues. The headset is falling off. There is a minor technical issue with the headset. It's sort of sliding off my head. May I please tighten them a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you would like to you review the pseudonym sheet that has been placed before you, and could you verify for us that it correctly lists your name and your last name along with the pseudonym, MLD21.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would then ask that you sign or initial the bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would move to introduce this into evidence under seal as the next available 1D Defence number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D10. ID10 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please state for the record what ethnicity you are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I'm an Orthodox Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now without telling us the precise location, could you tell us what municipality you live in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And where -- that is to say, in what municipality did you reside in the year 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could briefly go into private session I'd like to discuss some matters that would reveal the identity of the witness if done in open court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, we are in open session, so everything we say is being broadcast to the public; so I would caution you to be very careful not to reveal any identifying details about yourself. Now, upon your return to Visegrad, did there come to be a time when you were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: In May, all able-bodied men got assignments in the army or the reserve police forces. Invalids, the sick, and the elderly, stayed back in the factory, continued working there and made sure the place was still safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to yourself, did there come to be a time when you were personally mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Yes, at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know the date in May or ... any time-period that you make a reference to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Sometime in May. I don't remember the date. It may have been the 8th or the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the mobilisation, can you describe for us the process by which you and other able-bodied males from Visegrad were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Mobilisation call-ups were sent out by the recruitment office and people were categorised according to their military specialty the same criteria being used as had been used at the time by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, waiting for the transcript. Could you tell us after the mobilisation call-ups were sent out by the recruitment office what steps did persons like yourself have to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I responded to the call-up with my unit, and then my unit assigned me to the command security detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the command -- the security detail of the command. First of all, where was the command located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: The command was at Bikavac in the hotel. The hotel was being used for those purposes. Food was being stored there for all of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And without going into details that may identify you, can you please tell us what kind of tasks or assignments you performed at your command security post at the command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Personally providing security for the command, the facilities, and the physical items there. Primarily, in my case, it meant food.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As part of your duties, did you have occasion to come in contact with the persons at the command who were responsible for driving the food to the forces at the front lines and at their positions and distributing the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I would just help them with loading the stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Are you familiar with the names of the individuals who participated in driving the food in the van or truck to the various locations where the food needed to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you -- can you give us their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: There were a number of them. Mladen Petkoza, Josip, Stevo Milosavljevic, Milojko Vukovic, there quite a number of people involved. I can hardly be expected to provide all of their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if you please focus on two of them that you mentioned. You mentioned a gentleman named Josip. Do you recall what ethnicity or religious group Josip belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: He was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned another person, I'm sorry I can't see the transcript. The last name and the first name was Stevo, I think, what could you tell us about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Yes. He was a Serb. A driver with Centrotrans. He was married and had two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to these two individuals, Josip and Stevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: They were both killed. They drove over a mine, when they were taking food to some people who were at positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of what structure or force these individuals belonged to, Josip and Stevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: They belonged to the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving along, do you know a man named Vidoje Andric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I probably need to go into private session to ensure that my further questioning on this topic doesn't reveal the identity of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You've -- sir, you've detailed for us your encounters with Milan Lukic. Did you have occasion -- strike that. Let me ask you -- let me back up. Are you familiar with individual named Sladjan Simic, and if so, could you tell us who that man was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Sladjan Simic was a young man from Bosanska Jagodina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: During the war, what was his position, rank, or post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I don't know what his rank was. He led a group of scouts. The group included about ten men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say he led a group of scout, to what entity or structure did these scouts belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what can you tell us about your knowledge of any of the individuals who were members of this group of army scouts led by Sladjan Simic from Bosanska Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Well, their task was to reconnoitre the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I want to thank you on behalf of the Defence of Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, those are all the questions I have on direct examination for this witness, and I would pass the witness to the -- One moment. I apologise, Your Honours, yes, I'm finished with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is Dermot Groome. I'm going to ask you a few questions on behalf of the Prosecution. Could I ask that we go into private session, Your Honour. The first series of questions have to do with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, in the summary that we were given and in the statement that we were given about your evidence, we were advised that you were going to provide some evidence about the White Eagles; and I don't recall that you have given any on your direct examination, but I do want to ask you a couple of questions regarding paramilitary groups that may have been in and around Visegrad in 1992. Did you see any paramilitary formations in the town of Visegrad in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Lack of foundation as to paramilitary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What kind of foundation are you expecting?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The question expects that the witness understands what paramilitary means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you understand, Witness, what the term "paramilitary" means? I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You do? He does so let's proceed with the -- the answer. You were asked whether you saw any paramilitary formations in Visegrad, in the spring or summer of 1992. What is your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally did not see them, nor do I personally know anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, sir, from what you have described to us already, it seems that you were a person who was there the entire time and who would have with great frequency have passed through the centre part of the town. Is it your evidence that in the spring and summer of 1992, you did not see any paramilitary formations or paramilitaries in and around Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Let me repeat, I personally did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that had they been there, you would have been in a position to see them?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, just a minute. He followed on from what counsel said. Perhaps you might reformulate the question or move on, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, sir, correct me if I'm wrong. It seems to me that what you have testified to is that you would have -- if not on a daily basis, on a very regular basis have been in and around the centre of Visegrad; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Can you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you in and around the centre of Visegrad frequently during the spring and summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Well, the command was in town. That is a kilometre or two from the centre. That is the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you pass through the centre of town when you were going home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you pass in front of the new hotel next to the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How often would you pass in front of the new hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Perhaps once in two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If paramilitaries were staying at the new hotel, would you believe that you would have seen them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you -- I asked you about paramilitary formations. Did you ever, at any time, see an individual who you believed was not part of the regular police or part of the regular army but would have been an individual paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you go to the command in Bikavac every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Every second day, that is how my particular shift was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The command centre that you have spoken about, that was in the hotel in Bikavac; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Chamber has already heard evidence about a very serious fire where there was a significant loss of life just a few streets from the Bikavac hotel at the end of June. Do you recall seeing anything or hearing anything with respect to a -- a fire of that description in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it possible that you have heard or learned something, but you have since forgotten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, when you first began going to the Bikavac command post, would it be fair to say that there were still a large number of Muslim residents living in the Bikavac area; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: In the area -- I don't know that there was a single Muslim in the area of Bikavac at that time. When Murat actually opened the sluice gates on the dam, all the Muslims fled Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So is it your evidence that during the time that you were going to the Bikavac command centre that you did not see Muslim families in and around the area of Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see Muslim houses in Bikavac being burned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Both Serbian and Muslim houses were being set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And during what period of time did you see houses being burnt in the Bikavac area of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: That same year, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was it during the time that you were on duty at the Bikavac hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I cannot recall with precision, but it was around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that houses quite close to the Bikavac command centre were destroyed by fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: There was not a single house on fire around the command post, but there were some houses on fire in -- on the outskirts of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask you about your contact or how you came to be a witness. Can I ask you who first contacted you about being a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: A gentleman whose name I believe was -- got in touch with me. His name was Vlado, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I see that you're now referring to some notes that looks like a pad from a hotel. Are those some notes that you have from -- from a hotel stationery that you -- that you have made since coming to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you mind if I take a look at them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I have nothing. I just jotted down the names of people here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But you have referred to some notes that you have on hotel stationery. If they relate to this case, I would appreciate an opportunity to take a look at them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. If you hand them to the usher, then she will allow me to look at them, and I will work with an interpreter over the break to take a look at them. Sir, can you tell us the names of other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, pass them to the Defence and the Bench as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, while we are they're being shown I did happen to notice, even though I don't speak the language, that on the top of it is the name of the person who was discussed in closed session, the person that you have a very good recollection of what happened so so long ago. Why did you need to have his name written down on the -- the note paper, given your fine powers of recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I did so in order to have a concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you explain by what you mean by having a concept?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, a reminder. The witness also added: A reminder of whom I had been with in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, sir, I believe that when I asked you did you have any reminder of that event, you said that you had no reminder; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I didn't mean any reminder in a big way. I mean, this is nothing particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So is it your evidence that you recall this event almost 17 years ago, and the day before you give evidence about it, you make a reminder of the person you met, and you write his name down on this piece of paper; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I don't see what's disputable about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not disputing -- I'm just asking you -- am I stating what has happened here correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. You can interpret it any way you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of all the other members of the Defence team who you had contact with prior to coming to testify here today.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I was with Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many times did you meet with Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I think once, before I arrived in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And then did you meet him again after coming to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Once, in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever have any contact with a person by the name of Drago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever have contact with Milan Lukic's sister, Draginja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I don't even know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever have contact with a person by the name of Jelena Rasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No. I don't know her either.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to give you some names -- put some names to you and ask you do you know any of these people. Do you know a person by the name of Boban Simsic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you know about Boban Simsic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection as to the form of the question: Vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you know about Boban Simsic? I would agree, Mr. Groome, that is a vague question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How do you know Boban Simsic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I know his father, I know his mother; and I have known him ever since he was a small child.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever know him to be a member of a paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No, never, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How about a person by the name of Oliver Krsmanovic; do you know a person by that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Dragutin Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Djordje Sevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How about Niko Vujicic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How about a person by the name of Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: He was a waiter, and - excuse my language - an ordinary lush.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask that you be shown Exhibit P149. But before I do that, how many times between the first time you met Milan Lukic and the time that you had another encounter in August, how many times or with what frequency did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Very, very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, I have no further questions that I want to ask at this time. If I could just ask that the witness be kept in the building while -- and during the break I will have someone read the note, and I ask that I have an opportunity to ask some questions that may arise from what is written on the reminder note that the witness brought to court with him. But I have no further questions that I wish to ask at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not sure I understand the request, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the note that the witness says was a reminder that he brought to court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see, that note.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So just if I can have an opportunity to understand it. I may not have any questions arising from it, but in the event I do, I ask that the witness be kept in the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have one or two questions on redirect. I don't know if you want to do them now. I don't know when the break is with the new schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, we will take the break at 4.40.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We started at 3.10. So we take a break at 4.40.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again Mr. Witness, just to clear up some matters. I didn't have the B/C/S channel on, so I don't know how it was translated to you, but you were asked about your contacts with the Defence team; and you -- and you correctly indicated that we meant once there Visegrad, could you tell us, do you recall the meetings that we had in the hotel with VWS present these days at the hotel here in The Hague where are you staying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Yes, I remember those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you -- could you tell for the Trial Chamber with respect to the meeting that we had this morning where we were situated and where the VWS individual, I won't mention his name due to their policy, was situated while I was performing your proofing. The gentleman who let you use his phone to call home.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: We were sitting on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But that gentleman was present in the room with us, was -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is all I have on behalf of re-direct. I thank the witness again on behalf of the Milan Lukic, and I it leave it to Your Honours' discretion if he needs to stay. I move on to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What I'm inclined to do is take the break now, Mr. Groome, in order to facility the earliest departure of the witness. I would just take the break now and then you let us know whether you have any further questions, so in that case, the witness would return, yes? If you don't have any further questions, then let us know before the end of the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I understand you to do have a few more questions arising from your perusal of the note. Further Cross-examination by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just a few questions. Your Honour, I have a very draft translation that some of my staff were able to do over the course of the break. I would ask with the assistance of the usher if they could be distributed to both the Bench and the Defence counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, while that is being distributed, could I ask you when did you write these notes? Did you hear my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Today. An hour before I went to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were you with anyone when you wrote the note?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm going ask that you be given a photocopy of the note. I am going to ask that the original be tendered into evidence as a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P244, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, the first question I want to ask you is, is there two names that you wrote on this note on the top left-hand corner. Am I correct in saying that these men are now deceased?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: They're not -- they didn't die a natural death; they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But they both are dead today. They're -- both of them are no longer living; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic discussed these two names with you in private session. Is -- if I are were to mention their names and ask you something about these men here in open session would that compromise your identity or your security in any way?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for speculation. I would ask that we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Alarid is proceeding on the basis that it is better to err on the side of precaution. I would agree. Let's move into private --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might just be heard. I think all of us here place great value on the public nature of these proceedings. These are men that are dead for more than 15 years. If the witness has a reason to have some concern about mentioning those names in public session, then I have absolutely no objection to going into private session, but if the witness says there is no possibility that his security will be compromised then I don't see why we would be in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And again how could the witness be in a position to know that. It is only the person that recognises someone from an association that actually exposes the identity. The witness cannot know such a thing. On the err of caution, I still argue that we move into private.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is not my intention to ask about any association simply about how he knows how this man died.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Ask him the question, whether he -- in his view, his identify would be compromised. Please ask him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm interested in the first name more precisely. If I were to ask you what you know about that first man in open session, would that compromise your identity or cause you any fear for your security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you to take a look of the photocopy of the note you brought to court to refresh your memory. Can I ask you to read what is written directly after the names of the two men that we have just discussed in private session.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: All of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm just looking -- if you would read the top line, on the top right-hand corner. It begins with: "I met Milan."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: No. I introduced Milan to these other two. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So your note says that you introduced Milan to these other two. Is my memory correct of your evidence that you were introduced to Milan on this occasion. Was that not your testimony in direct examination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: It was with these two men that I met Milan.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, this could be read both ways. It was with these two men that I was introduced to Milan or that I met Milan; but also I introduced Milan to these two men. Both reading are possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, so is it your evidence that you needed to write this reminder that you met Milan Lukic with these two men and their names spelled out, just hours before you testified here in court.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now the second line of the -- could I ask you to read the second line in the -- in the note, beginning with: "I was looking" -- I'm sorry, could I ask you read to the names, that's the part that I'm more interested in. The names beginning with Mile Bozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Gogic, Nedeljko; Joksimovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you please say the name of the last person again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Bozic, Mile; Gogic, Nedeljko; or Joksimovic, Timotije. They were from the same village but I didn't know if they were together. I wanted to track down any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you needed to write -- again you needed to write a reminder of who they were that you were seeking to give sugar and coffee to, just a few hours before you testified here in court. You nodded your head, but we need to have an audible answer to complete the record.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: It's not like I needed to, but there you go, I did. Just in order to jog my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And finally, sir, I just ask you to read the line that begins with: "In August." Could you read that for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: Later he was in the army with Sladjan Simic. In August, he was at Jelasice. This is the time when those people were killed at Jelasice.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you that you given a fine-point pen. I'm just going to ask you at the bottom of the paper that you have before you, the photocopy could I ask you just to re-write the line that says, "I was looking for someone from the reserve force of the police." Could I just ask you just in your own hand write that somewhere on the photocopy of the -- could I ask to be a fine-point pen. I have one here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection as to relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me find out what the objection, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection as to relevance. Where is this going?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The witness will write it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, would you please just somewhere in the blank portion underneath the photocopy just copy over the line that reads: "I was looking for someone from the reserve force of the police."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If I could just take a quick look at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And then pass it to the Bench and to counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you and I put to you quite plainly that you do not have any recollection of the events that you testified to because they never happened. They're a fabrication, and the note that you brought into court or to remind you was necessary to remind you of what the fabrication is. Do you understand what I'm putting to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD21
utterances.text: That's not true, sir. You don't know what it was like to be in my shoes during those days. What I heard with my own ears, what I saw with my own eyes, that was the account that I gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry, I'd ask that -- I tender that other exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes it is admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P245, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, do you wish to ask anything in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't think so. I thank the witness on behalf of the Milan Lukic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. That concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, that should be MLD9.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I believe it is 19. I believe you mean 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe he is actually also number 9 and 19. He has received protective measures twice. According to my records, we had disclosed the statement under 9, so that is how I picked that pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are we settled as to who is being called, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's the same witness, apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're waiting just so there is not greater confusion when it comes time and in final submissions, I just ask Mr. Ivetic to clarify. I'm looking at a filing here from 7 January 2009, where a person whose last name begins with a K is identified as MLD19. Is that the person who is being called now and I think it might make more sense to refer to him by the pseudonym that has been used more recently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, can you clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I would like to do it in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir. My name is Dan Ivetic, and I will be asking you questions today on behalf of the Defence of Milan Lukic. I'm going to be referring to you by the pseudonym of MLD19, in line with the protective measures that have been granted to you. First of all, I would ask the assistance of the court usher to distribute and then present in front of you a pseudonym sheet that have I prepared. And then once that sheet is before you, sir, I would ask you to review the same and to verify that it accurately sets forth your identifying details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you review the pseudonym sheet that has been placed in front you and verify whether, in fact, it accurately states your identification details.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm the data is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would ask that you sign and -- sign the bottom of the form; and, Your Honours, I would ask that it be admitted in evidence under seal as the next available 1D number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D11, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please, for the record, state your ethnic affiliation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now without going into details that would -- that would disclose your identity, for the record, could you tell us in which municipality you reside today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Visegrad municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And where did you reside; that is to say, in which municipality did you reside in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: In Uzice municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go into private session for the next several questions will deal with personal matters of the witness's identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could focus on the outbreak of tensions in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Were you mobilised; and, if so, could you give us the details of your mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I was engaged to drive my truck. The former Yugoslav army actually recruited me to do that; namely, transport different materials because some extremists had demolished some tunnels and roads; so they were unable to clear up the roads and the tunnels, and they had us come with our trucks from Visegrad in order to clear the site and cut away the rubble and the other material there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say you were engaged to clear the site and cut away the rubble. What specific tasks did you undertake while mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, we worked near Dobrun, which is to say at the very border with Serbia. The road had caved in, and the tunnels had been blown up by unknown extremists who had placed explosives and blown up the tunnels.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say that the army had come to you -- to us, with our trucks from Visegrad. At that time, were you residing or employed in Visegrad municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: No. We would just occasionally go because they were there. We were nearby. We would go to the barracks in Kremna where we would sleep, and we travelled with army vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what kind of vehicle registration plates were on your truck that you utilised at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: It was G, which is a Z with a mark above it, with civilian licence plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Any particular republic of the former SFRY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: In Bosnia, they were registered in Visegrad, and Visegrad did not issue its own licence plates so that they bore Gorazde, GZ, were the licence plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you remain so mobilised and so engaged in the Yugoslav army's business the entire duration of the convict or did that change at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: We were engaged over the first month of the conflict. Sometime until the 16th of May, when the army departed the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Waiting for the translation and the transcript. And after the army departed -- or when the army departed the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, what did you do at that point in time, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I went to Serbia to live, because there no longer -- it was no longer secure in Bosnia. No one knew who was in power nor what was happening in that republic, or in the town in which I had been living, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you -- you say you went to Serbia to live. Did you go alone, did you go with someone else? How did you -- how did you go to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I went there with my family. I loaded our things onto a vehicle. I rented out a room in Uzice, and I lived there with my wife and my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what happened with your truck? Did it remain behind in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: No. I drove the truck there, and I continued to work in Serbia, because that was the former Yugoslavia; and I already had some contract with the some companies for whom I undertook transport work, and I continued to work in that capacity in Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can go in private session I believe the next couple questions are of a nature that might reveal the identity of the witness to third parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, during the time-period that you lived in Uzice in 1992, did you -- did there come a time where you met or encountered Milan Lukic during that time-period, during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Yes. Two men came, one of whom was Milan Lukic. He introduced himself as Milan Lukic. And the other one was a policeman. Both were in uniforms. They were also carrying batons and had on camouflage uniforms, with pips on their shoulders. One day they came outside my flat. I knew this first man. His name was Vidoje Andric, and the said gentleman Milan Lukic actually introduced himself to me on that occasion. I did not know him personally before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, go ahead. Continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: They asked me to go back to Bosnia, because some sort of a mobilisation had already started. Mobilisation for war. They told me that a certain commander, Tomic, had sent instructions to the effect that they were to call me to go to -- to go back to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the time-period or date when this encounter took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, it was sometime around June, the 20th or the 22nd of June or thereabouts. I just happened to remember the date, because on the 13th of June, the husband was killed of the lady who was the witness at my wedding. That's why I remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go into private session so as not to identify this relative of -- he said "kum," but I see something different in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I think you had already described the uniforms worn by these individuals. Did you have occasion to see the automobile that they came in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: No, I did not see the automobile because there were many automobiles in the street, and I could not tell which particular vehicle they had come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the time that they came to your home in Uzice in June of 1992, were you aware of any mobilisations in effect for Visegrad residents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I wasn't, because I thought that that was a done matter. The -- that the war actually was over, the army had withdrawn, and that's what I was thinking at the time. I did not suppose that there would be any continuation of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Andric or Mr. Lukic take you into custody and force you to come back to Visegrad with them on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, given the fact that you knew this Andric fellow, he did not insist very strongly on returning me to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What -- what did you tell them as to your response to the mobilisation request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I told them that I had already contracts for some deals, that I had deadlines to adhere to, that I had signed some contracts with firms with companies, and that if I did not actually fulfil my obligations I would be -- there would be penalties for me to pay and things like that. That I could go then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, return to Visegrad in compliance with the mobilisation call-up or summons at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: No, not that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to return to Visegrad after the war for any reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I returned because the conditions in Serbia were no longer favourable for a normal life, so war also broke out then. It was the time for us to go back to wherever we came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have a reference in time as to when it was that you went back to Visegrad after the war: A month, a time-period, a season, a year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: It was in 1994. In early 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you remain in Visegrad from 1994 onwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I remained in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: During the intervening time-period after you returned to Visegrad; that is, post-1994. Did you have occasion at any point in time to ever see the man who had come to your home with Vidoje Andric who had been introduced to you as Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, actually, I did not see him, because I was working, repairing some forest roads. I was engaged by the army as a machine operator. The machinery that was used to repair these roads, so that I didn't have much occasion to -- I didn't have much contact with those people. We worked until late into the evening. Then we would spend the night in the barracks and then go home -- didn't go home, so that I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what about after the war? Did you have occasion to ever see Milan Lukic again after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Yes. I worked in his house for his father. They had bought a house, and I was excavating, doing excavations there for a garage near his home. I also moved some earth there and carted it away with my truck, and that's when I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And where was there house of his father located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: It was some 600 or 700 metres distance from the new bridge, over the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you have any -- any reference in time as to when this took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Ah, well, 1996, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And apart from the time during the war when he came to your house in Uzice, and apart from this time after the war, when you were assisting to constructs a garage at his father's home, did you have occasion to encounter Milan Lukic at any other point in time after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, yes. He owned a pub that I sometimes went to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, for the record, could you identify for us where this pub that he -- that he ran, where it was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: It the centre of town, near the municipality building, about 150 metres being the distance between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for your time and your answers to my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions in direct for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I'm from the Prosecution, and I would like to ask you a couple of questions. When is the first time that you were ever contacted by anyone from the Defence of Milan Lukic about possibly testifying here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Summer last year.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And do you recall the name of the person or persons who first contacted you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I don't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Was there more than one person; and where did you meet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: We met in Visegrad. There was a single person. The name, I think, was Boris.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is very standard cross-examination for a witness. Asking about the circumstances when they were first contacted to give testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes I would agree, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would now object to the characterisation as to this being standard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Never mind, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, when you met in Visegrad can you tell us where you met? Was it at someone's house or was it in a pub? And the person that you met, was it a male or a female?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: A male called Boris, as I said. We met in the courtyard outside the Visegrad hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And is that -- was it at that point in time that you gave a statement, a written statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: The next time he came was the time I gave a statement, not that first day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you gave the statement, did you personally write out the statement; or was the statement written out for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I wrote it down myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you told the Defence in your statement everything that you were going to testify about; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection. Cause for really a legal presentation and speculation as to what he is going testify about. The Defence presents witnesses and upon learning what they know, presents a witness as the -- without a foundation as to what he knew of the purposes for that statement being taken, I don't think that the question is proper.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I will withdraw that question and ask another one, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever tell this person who came to see you that you were going to testify about your knowledge of the good deeds and acts of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I wasn't told anything about the deeds and acts of Milan Lukic. They wanted to know about my goodwill to appear as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. But my question to you is: Did you ever tell them that you would talk about good deeds and acts of Milan Lukic? Did you tell them you would say those things?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection as to relevance. Lack of foundation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you ever tell team that you were going -- did you ever tell them that you would testify about the intimidation an actions of Bosnian authorities against Defence witnesses who were to meet and sign statements? Did you ever tell them that you would testify to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: May we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand the nature of the -- Ms. Sartorio' questioning. However I would like to point out to the Court that we filed our 65 ter summary before we ever met with this witness. So this is based on a broad understanding. It is for notice purposes only. It was only after personally meeting with the witness whether we were able to ascertain what the witness could or could not testify to. I would object to the line of questioning as being improper without lack of foundation, unduly suggestive, and otherwise spurious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness answer the question, and we must move on quickly, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. May we go move public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, public session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall my last question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I do. But I can't define your question. What is the question? Am I expected to talk about his deeds or misdeeds? I was in no position to know what it was that he had done at all. Good or bad. Therefore, I can hardly be expected to talk about it, can I?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I asked another question, and if you could listen carefully to my question. My question was: Did you ever tell the person whom you met from the Defence that you could testify about the intimidation and actions of Bosnian authorities against Defence witnesses who were to meet and sign statements. Did you ever tell them that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And one more similar question and that's it. I will move on. Sir, did you -- did you ever tell anyone from the Defence that you could testify that Milan Lukic saved the lives of the daughters of Behija Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I just would like to ask you a couple of questions about Uzice, which is where you lived in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I believe you testified on direct that you -- you went to Serbia on the 16th of May, because of the conflict that was going on. Is that -- that your -- recollection of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Yes. On the 16th of May, the Army of Yugoslavia left, and I left as part of that convoy. I left Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And so how far is Uzice, where you were living, from the municipality of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: 77 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So were you surprised when two men showed up at your door, asking for you to return to Visegrad and be mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, yes. I had not been in time to be involved in the conflict and that was the reason that I left Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, in fact, you never -- you did not go back to Visegrad with those two men, did you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then I believe you testified that the next time you saw Milan Lukic was long after the war was over -- or, let me paraphrase, it was 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Yes, when I returned from Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So the one and only time that you saw Milan Lukic during the conflict was on that date that you say he came to your house. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Let me ask you, are you related to either Milan Lukic or Sredoje Lukic in any way, from any -- any family relations?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My client is not mentioned in direct examination, so I don't see any base for foundation any question and mentioning of my client. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think we have been -- we have been there before, haven't we? Or we have been over that ground before, and I don't see anything improper in the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I believe the witness answered no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You said you were not related to either Milan Lukic or Sredoje. Is that your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not related to either of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know who Sredoje Lukic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, I know nothing about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Objection. Your Honour. This witness already gave clear answer related to Sredoje Lukic. That he doesn't know anything about him. I don't see the basis for further questions related to my client. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I believe he has answered sufficiently on that issue. So please move on Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That should also be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you some questions about when Milan Lukic and Mr. Andric showed up at your house. Can you describe in detail what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: They had a sort of camouflage uniform, blue, police with belts, handcuffs, a gun, and a truncheon, small guns, short-barrelled, and truncheon, club, whatever it's called.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Were they wearing any type of hats or caps or anything on their heads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Caps. On their shoulders with the three-colour flag insignia. These were caps that we referred to as the French caps, or berets. I believe that is the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And was there any type of emblem or insignia on the caps or berets that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, I said it, didn't I? The three-coloured flag: Red, white, blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, you said that that was on their shoulder. And my question to you was: Was there any insignia or emblem on the cap, not the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: It was on the caps, the front side of the caps and they wore these caps sort of tucked in under their shoulder straps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, had you seen these types of uniforms before, on other persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, this was the kind worn by Serbia's police, what we referred to as intervention units. But the colours were slightly different, different hues. Still blue but a different shade of blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us what you meant by "intervention units"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: These are specialised units, a bit like riot police, and they're specially trained to perform some particular military missions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And did you know any other members of this so-called intervention unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection. Your Honour, misstated the evidence. He did not indicate that they were members of an intervention unit, specific at page 59, lines 10 through 11 he said: The uniforms were the kind worn by Serbia's police, what we called them French units, but the colours were slightly different.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Perhaps you will reformulate then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So you said that the colours were like the ones worn by the intervention unit. So it your testimony that this what they were -- the uniform that Milan Lukic and Mr. Andric were wearing were not -- that they were not of the intervention unit, that they were not from that unit because it was a different type of uniform. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I said that, didn't I? Not the same colour. Not the same pattern. The stripes on that uniform. Not the same as those other ones that you mentioned, the intervention ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Which -- which uniforms had stripes? The ones that Milan Lukic was wearing or the ones from the intervention unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Both types of uniform had stripes, but they were different. The shade is different. One is a deeper shade of blue and the other, paler.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So I go back to a question that I asked a few moments ago. Did you ever see anyone else or did you know anyone else who wore the same uniforms as those two men wore that night you saw them, in Uzice. Can you give us the names of any other persons whom you've seen wearing those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: No. I didn't know any of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, do you know how Mr. Andric was employed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I didn't know what it was that he did. I know that before the war he was a karate coach in a club or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, may we go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute Ms. Sartorio. Mr. Alarid, may I ask you, do you have witnesses lined up for the rest of the evening?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have one more that should be here on the premises, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On the premises?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just one -- just a couple of more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, just one more question. You never committed any crimes with Milan Lukic, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Working backwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's remain in private.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, with regard to the issue of the manner in which your testimony was disclosed on 65 ter summary that was filed in, I believe, November, do you recall when it was that you and I met in Visegrad? What month or time of year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. It was late December.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when I met with you in Visegrad, did I inquire of you about the intervention of SIPA and the incident involving a witness to the saving of Behija Zukic's daughters by Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer. No, you didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did we discuss that individual in our meeting in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did we -- did we discuss that individual's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, this is going outside the scope of the cross-examination. I didn't ask him about this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is directly within the bounds of the cross-examination provided by the Prosecution. They're asking about our bases for the references to intervention that Behija Zukic is related to. And unless I can lead, I have to lay a foundation, so to lay a foundation I have to ask the questions from A to Z. I have to proceed in the manner that I'm the manner that I'm proceeding to get to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very quickly I understand we must break now because the tape is it running out. But let me just hear quickly, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this particular individual is not in the 65 ter summary. I think that counsel is limited to the question that I asked on cross; and, furthermore, he is continuing to lead. So I object on both grounds that is beyond the scope of cross and it's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll rule it on my return. 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio, my ruling is that the matter does arise, and it is an appropriate for counsel to lay the foundation and proceed. Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: May I continue then. Are you finished -- may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have also tried to -- I tried to short-circuit my questioning on that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What did you tell me about whether you would be able to testify as to what they knew, as to this incident involving Behija Zukic's daughters. What did you tell me as to whether you would be able to testify as to what they knew.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD19
utterances.text: Well, I can't really tell you what they knew. It's something that only they know about. I didn't talk to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, and on behalf of the Defence of Milan Lukic -- I guess we go into open session, Your Honours. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, on behalf of the Defence of Milan Lukic, I thank you for coming here to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your testimony and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Next witness is MLD22, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While the witness is being called, if I might raise a few matters perhaps make efficient use of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first matter I wish to bring to your attention I must say I'm deeply troubled by this situation where the witness -- we're provided a 65 ter summary, and then the witness does not testify about what is in the summary but is -- testifies about something entirely different. Mr. Alarid has given an explanation to that, but just looking over our records, the original 65 ter summary for this witness was provided in November. It was a very terse one or two sentence summary. We now hear that Mr. Ivetic met with the witness in December and on the 5th of January is when we received a current 65 ter summary, which is after Defence counsel have met with the person; and in it, what we've been preparing our cross-examination according to, is an indication that man testify as to the daughters of Behija Zukic and his knowledge of how Milan Lukic saved their lives, and that he will also testify about intimidation and actions of SIPA and Bosnian authorities. We're entitled to be put on accurate notice of a witness, what a witness will testify about. Given that this summary is provided after the Defence have spoken to this witness, I must object to what has happened here today and I would ask that if any other changes to 65 ter summaries that we be given notice as soon as possible about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This was in closed session, so if can he have a redaction of everything that was said in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
