utterances.text: Why does it need to be in closed session if nothing that's in the 65 ter summary is anything that this man knows about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: His testimony was in private session. It is my understand when testimony is in private session discussions relating to that testimony are in private session. Those are the Rules that I have operated for under ten years here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I didn't hear that, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The discussion of the witness as to this incident was in private session. It is my understanding that has been the course of practice for over the ten years that I've been here that when testimony is in closed session or private session it is not -- it is not brought up in open session. It needs to be done in private session or the same status session as the original testimony was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not talking about any of the testimony. This was Mr. Alarid, I believe, asked to go into private session to give his explanation. I believe it is up to the Court to decide what needs to properly be in private session. I will be guided by the Court whether any of this needs be in private session. I believe it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't see the need for that to be in private session. Yes, so the -- Mr. Alarid, was your response that you haven't given notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the real problem has been raised ad nauseum I don't need to give another speech as to the limited resources we have had in case and how we've tried to put this case together. We're doing the best we can. We compiled these 65 ters before we talked to many people based on lose understandings. I apologise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. We need to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The other matter I want to bring to your attention is more than a month ago on 20 January the Court ordered that the Defence apply the Prosecution with, quote, complete details of all the remaining witnesses, including their names, correctly spelled, their dates of birth, and the father's names. While we have been given this information with respect to the witness this is week, we have not been given this information for the remainder of the witnesses. We are doing our best to try not ask for the Court for any adjournment to do investigation by it's imperative that the Prosecution have the information that it's entitled to. I'm, therefore, asking the Court to order Defence counsel to provide all of this information by the time we start our session tomorrow. I think that's a very reasonable and overdue request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I do so order. Let the witness be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit and you may begin. Mr Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, as you know my name is Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the attorney for Milan Lukic. I will be dealing your examination today. I'm going to have to refer to you by the pseudonym MLD22 and protect your identity in accord with the protective measures that have been issued by the Trial Chamber for you. As soon as you get situated there I will ask the assistance of the court usher to show you a pseudonym sheet that has been prepared which should have your name and the pseudonym MLD22 on it. Once the same makes its way to you, I would ask you to review it and then verify that the information contained therein as to yourself is true and accurate. Can you verify that the information contained therein as to yourself is true and accurate, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In that case I could -- I would ask that you sign the sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would tender this document into evidence as the next available exhibit number under seal for the 1D Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D12 [sic], under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that accurate, 1D12?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D112, Your Honours. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, for the record could you state your ethnicity, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us if you have ever had the occasion to testify before, in legal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: No, never. This is my first time before this Tribunal, or any Tribunal, for that matter. My first testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And I know you had a difficult flight to get here, so if at any time if you need to take a break, please let me know and we will try to accommodate you. Now, without revealing the exact location can you tell us where it is that you live, what municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And where did you live, in which municipality did you live in 1992; again, without giving the precise address.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to move into private session to discuss the personal details of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, turning to the outbreak of hostilities in Visegrad in 1992, were you mobilised at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: I was mobilised on or about the 19th of March, 1992, and was sent to Bikavac, the restaurant there. The restaurant had sustained a great deal of damage, and I used my technical expertise to get the place up and running again, clear it up, to make sure the conditions were again sanitary and safe for everyone. I was responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could we back up and could you please confirm for us the date when it was that you were mobilised and sent to the Bikavac restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: The date was the 19th of March -- May. May, I'm sorry, the 19th of May. My apologies, but time seems to have left a mark on my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: By what structure were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: Visegrad Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say he were sent to Bikavac, what particular -- what was the particular nature of that location? What was it called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: It's the Visegrad Bikavac hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what purpose did that structure serve during the -- during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: It housed the command and the forward section of the medical unit defence preparations. What do I know? I only know that I was in charge of sanitation there and just in case of something sordid going on, such as war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to be posted elsewhere in addition to the command at Bikavac; and, if so, where were you posted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: I was seconded to the Guards Service. It was the building security detail; for example, when men took off to go back home to get a bath or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I understand with respect to that building, the Bikavac command. But were you posted or assigned to go anywhere else as part of your duties within the Territorial Defence, anywhere else, any other geographical location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: My apologies. After Bikavac, I went to Zupa because a male nurse had been killed there, so I went to stand in for the nurse who had been killed there, in the village of Rujiste. Stevo Grujic was the name of the male nurse who had been killed, so the unit dispatched me to go there and stand in for him, replace him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Where precisely was your -- was the position of your units in relation to the village of Rujiste in the Zupa valley?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: The position was to the north-east of the village, near the road that was just above the village of Rujiste. There was a privately owned cottage that was there, and that's where we were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the course of the time that you spent in the village of Rujiste, did you have occasion to meet Milan Lukic or his parents at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: Well, Milan's parents were living down in the village. And every time they went to Visegrad, they had to pass us on the way. And then for a while, food was taken there, and they were getting food. That was a problem, the food. I would see Milan whenever he came to see his parents to make sure whether they needed anything, such as medicines if they were ill, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: Any human being would go and see how their parents were doing so it was only expected that he would as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if you could -- if you could clarify for us, where were the enemy forces located in relation to Rujiste and the position of your units in that region.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: Our unit was securing the right river-bank of the Drina from Krusevo on to [indiscernible], the nearest Serb villages. In fact, they were just holding the line there, to make sure there were no clashes or enemy provocations. What should I call that? Clashes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you know Milan Lukic prior to meeting him in Rujiste while he was visiting his parents during the time-period that you were posted there with your unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you have occasion to see Milan Lukic while in the town centre during the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: I saw him with some policemen, with the police commander, wearing a police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to -- you say you saw him with the police commander. Which police commander are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: I think the police commander in Visegrad was called Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall prior to the outbreak of the war what position or occupation this Tomic had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: He was a policeman in Visegrad, working with the police station in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What kind of uniforms did Milan Lukic and this police commander Tomic have on the times that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: Milan Lukic and the police commander Tomic had blue uniforms. The kind worn by the police at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would the two of these individuals be alone or in the company of others at the times that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22
utterances.text: The commander always had at least two escorts. I'm a medical help person myself. I don't know about the way this worked in their line of work, but I would always see the commander with two escorts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your Honours, that's all I have for direct examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I'm to ask it if I could commence my cross-examination tomorrow. I think it will be in the interest of judicial economy in any event. Hopefully I can cut down what I have at the moment. One of the problems has been, Your Honours, that I was to an extend incommunicado with the first part of the session today because of the technical difficulties. So I'm not aware of the testimony that proceeded my entrance into the courtroom. So it would be helpful if could I go through that. There may well be some things there that can I incorporate into my cross-examination. So could I just ask that my cross-examination commence tomorrow. We're making good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, very well. We'll adjourn until 2.15 tomorrow. And I'm to say that next week, the sitting will be Tuesday to Friday. Tuesday to Friday. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure what the impetus was behind that decision only that we've already arranged for Mr. Vladimir Rasic to come in Sunday, and we expected to get him out on Monday, and because of his employment we were hoping to get him done on Monday. Would there be any possibility of sort of flipping that and making Friday off if that were the case, because -- I don't know if that is feasible. Just consider it, Your Honour, and maybe we can discuss it tomorrow, but that's just what I wanted to let you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thanks. We'll consider it. Thanks. We're adjourned.
